sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球排名前列的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内开展合作与创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学使命的一部分，旨在促进所有生物的生活质量。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I want to be careful not to overstate what it means for a building to die.
sentences.zh: 我想谨慎一点，不要夸大一座建筑消亡的意义。

sentences.en: A building's worth is an infinitesimal fraction of the worth of a person's life.
sentences.zh: 建筑的价值与人的生命价值相比，只是微不足道的一小部分。

sentences.en: Even two buildings don't even move the needle in comparison to real human laws.
sentences.zh: 即使是两座建筑，在真正的人类生命面前也根本无足轻重。

sentences.en: But a building is still a living thing in a way.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，建筑依然是有生命的。

sentences.en: It breathes.
sentences.zh: 它会呼吸。

sentences.en: And it moves.
sentences.zh: 它会移动。

sentences.en: This movement makes a sound.
sentences.zh: 这种移动会发出声音。

sentences.en: The structural engineer who designed the World Trade Center Towers says that the people working inside couldn't feel this movement of the towers swaying in the breeze.
sentences.zh: 设计世界贸易中心双子塔的结构工程师说，在里面工作的人感觉不到大楼在微风中摇曳的这种移动。

sentences.en: But they could hear it.
sentences.zh: 但他们能听到。

sentences.en: Often, buildings speak to you.
sentences.zh: 通常，建筑会与你对话。

sentences.en: What happens in a tall building is that, in the wind, as the building moves, the floor above moves with respect to the floor below.
sentences.zh: 在高层建筑中发生的情况是，当风吹过，建筑发生位移时，楼上相对于楼下会产生移动。

sentences.en: My full name is Leslie E.
sentences.zh: 我的全名是莱斯利·E·

sentences.en: Robertson.
sentences.zh: 罗伯逊。

sentences.en: I'm a structural engineer, and I was responsible for the design of the World Trade Center.
sentences.zh: 我是一名结构工程师，负责了世界贸易中心的设计工作。

sentences.en: This cassette tape was one of many that we took during the construction and later occupation of the building.
sentences.zh: 这盘磁带是我们在这座建筑施工及后来投入使用期间录制的众多磁带之一。

sentences.en: For each cycle of oscillation of the building, we hear two creaking noises.
sentences.zh: 建筑每摆动一个周期，我们就能听到两声吱吱作响的声音。

sentences.en: And therefore, if you have a tape of it, you can then measure rather precisely the frequency of oscillation of the building itself.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你有录音，就可以相当精确地测量出建筑本身的振荡频率。

sentences.en: It takes ten seconds for a World Trade Center to go through one cycle of oscillation.
sentences.zh: 世界贸易中心完成一个振荡周期需要十秒钟。

sentences.en: This concludes the recording at the 67th floor, Tower 8, Projection Room.
sentences.zh: 8号楼67层放映室的录音到此结束。

sentences.en: Do you know what I can say about it?
sentences.zh: 你知道我对此能说什么吗？

sentences.en: I used to be extremely sound sleeper.
sentences.zh: 我曾经是一个睡眠质量极好的人。

sentences.en: I'm the kind of put my head down the pillow and go to sleep and sleep for just a short while and get up and go back to work or do whatever.
sentences.zh: 我属于那种头一沾枕头就能睡着，睡一会儿就能起来继续工作或做任何事的人。

sentences.en: But it's kind of not like that anymore.
sentences.zh: 但现在已经不是那样了。

sentences.en: I just, but I don't have images of the Trade Center in my dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我只是……但我梦里并没有世贸中心的画面。

sentences.en: I do wake up with the thoughts in my head that I do, but it's sort of like instantaneous.
sentences.zh: 我确实会带着脑子里的想法醒来，但那感觉就像是瞬间发生的。

sentences.en: And then I, as you wipe your eyes, you wipe the thought out of your mind.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你揉揉眼睛，就把那个念头从脑海中抹去了。

sentences.en: People keep saying, well, you did everything you could have done.
sentences.zh: 人们总是说，你已经尽了你所能做的一切。

sentences.en: The design was the best it could be.
sentences.zh: 设计已经是当时能做到的最好的了。

sentences.en: And, you know, all those thoughts, which are nice.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，那些想法都很暖心。

sentences.en: But I guess ultimately the responsibility for the criteria for the Trade Center, those were my decisions.
sentences.zh: 但我认为归根结底，世贸中心设计标准的责任，那些都是我的决定。

sentences.en: And the fact that they stood up as long as they did was because we had designed the project for the impact of the 707 aircraft.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们能屹立那么久，是因为我们按照波音707飞机的撞击标准设计了这个项目。

sentences.en: And we had a great team working on the project.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个很棒的团队在负责这个项目。

sentences.en: And they did what they were supposed to do.
sentences.zh: 他们完成了他们应该做的工作。

sentences.en: They stood up under the impact.
sentences.zh: 它们在撞击下屹立不倒。

sentences.en: And while it's true that the plane that hit it was a bit heavier and was flying a whole lot faster,
sentences.zh: 虽然撞击它的飞机确实更重一些，飞行速度也快得多，

sentences.en: and therefore a whole lot more energy was put into the building,
sentences.zh: 因此有更多的能量作用在建筑上，

sentences.en: I think it's a tribute to the people who worked on the project, that they did as well as they did.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，建筑表现得如此出色，是对项目参与人员的一种致敬。

sentences.en: And yet I know as well as I'm here right this moment that the buildings could have been made more stalwart, sure.
sentences.zh: 然而，我此刻非常清楚，建筑当然可以造得更坚固。

sentences.en: They could have been made stronger, and they could have stood up longer.
sentences.zh: 它们本可以造得更强，本可以屹立更久。

sentences.en: And that was my decision.
sentences.zh: 那是我的决定。

sentences.en: And that's, I think, in a sense, I can't be faulted because the structure is performed in many ways admirably.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在某种意义上，我不能被指责，因为结构在许多方面表现得令人钦佩。

sentences.en: But there's always that nagging thought that maybe you should have done something else.
sentences.zh: 但总有一个挥之不去的念头，觉得也许你应该做点别的。

sentences.en: And that I can't just push that out of my head.
sentences.zh: 那个念头我无法从脑海中抹去。

sentences.en: This episode of 99% Invisible was produced by the Kitchen Sisters, Davia Nelson and Nikki Silva, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 本期《99%隐形》由“厨房姐妹”（Kitchen Sisters）达维亚·尼尔森和尼基·席尔瓦，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯共同制作。

sentences.en: It's comprised of extracts and outtakes from the Peabody Award-winning Sonic Memorial Project produced in 2002.
sentences.zh: 它由2002年制作的皮博迪奖获奖作品《声音纪念项目》的片段和未收录内容组成。

sentences.en: A new 10th anniversary edition of the Sonic Memorial Project, which is narrated by my literary hero, Paul Oster,
sentences.zh: 《声音纪念项目》十周年纪念版由我崇拜的文学偶像保罗·奥斯特担任旁白，

sentences.en: is going to be playing on public radio stations around the country.
sentences.zh: 即将在全国各地的公共广播电台播出。

sentences.en: It is very much worth your time to seek out.
sentences.zh: 非常值得你花时间去寻找收听。

sentences.en: You can find out more at kitchensisters.org.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 kitchensisters.org。

sentences.zh: 本节目《99%隐形》由 Lunar 提供支持，他们用创造力创造改变。

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW 91.7 Local Public Radio in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 这是旧金山 KALW 91.7 本地公共广播电台的一个项目。

sentences.en: The American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 旧金山美国建筑师协会。

sentences.en: And the Center for Architecture and Design.
sentences.zh: 以及建筑与设计中心。

sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 99percentinvisible.org。
